title: How the world's stock markets pass the baton

lines.text: The stock market never really sleeps. It passes the baton around the world, every single day.
It starts in Asia. Tokyo opens while most of America is asleep.
Then Europe picks it up. London opens at 3 a.m. Eastern time.
lines.say: Then Europe picks it up. London opens at three a.m. Eastern time.

lines.text: And the U.S. runs the last leg. The New York Stock Exchange trades from 9:30 to 4 Eastern.
lines.say: And the U.S. runs the last leg. The New York Stock Exchange trades from nine thirty to four, Eastern.

lines.text: That's why big news overnight in Asia or Europe can move U.S. stocks before most people wake up.
So when we say markets reacted overnight, now you know which runners carried it.
That's the money. See you at the next bell.
